verdict: PARTIALLY ALIGNED: the strategy, the science-safety design and the arithmetic are sound, but the master runbook (07), the cost docs (08) and parts of section 13 were never updated with the founder's later decisions. Following them today would produce a non-compliant video.
summary: The project is partially aligned. The building blocks are mostly correct. All 26 offline selftests pass. About 120 cost figures recompute correctly. Science comes only from fixtures, approvals are bound to hashes, ultracode is refused, entitlement stays on the platform, and nothing from the ChatGPT source is missing (checked by hash). The failure is at integration. The checklist the founder is told to follow still renders 16:9 masters. It has no storyboard gate, no AI-voice disclosure step and no ultracode rule, and it still counts review as cash. Section 13 lets Reels skip their second approval and puts academic approval after rendering. The cue-sheet builder's output fails its own schema. Most of the fixes are edits that carry decisions already made into 07, 08 and 13, plus one code fix. After that, ship one vertical lesson end to end before writing more documentation.

lens_verdicts.verdict: Partially aligned. The new layers (11 PLAYBOOK, 12 animations, 13 strong-to-cheap) fit the goals well. They make everything vertical, protect the Super Teacher persona with negative tests against hype, take science only from fixtures, ban ultracode, add a storyboard gate and budget ledgers, keep two human approvals, and measure learning instead of virality. The selftests and the §7.13 arithmetic check out. But the master runbook in 07, where the ROOT README sends the founder first, was never updated to match those decisions; they appear only as one addendum and a set of proposed amendments. Following 07/03 and 11_MASTER_CHECKLIST today would render 16:9 lessons, skip any AI-voice disclosure, skip the human storyboard gate before paid generation, launch English-only and route Assamese through TTS, and default to curated rather than the first three free chapters. It would also show a cost picture in which review is the dominant cash cost, which contradicts the $0-review decision. Inside 13, Reels lose their second approval (§5.7), and the cost floors assume TTS while the playbook requires a human teacher performance for every full lesson. The direction is right, but the two critical and six major propagation gaps need to be closed in 07 (and the ROOT README) before the runbook can be used to produce a correct, compliant video.

Partially aligned. Within section 12, the core numbers line up: loudness, vertical type minimums derived from RD-01/RD-18, the 3-loop authoring cap, ultracode refusal, harness-copy integrity and the skill registry (72 rows, all owners present). These are backed by passing self-tests and correct arithmetic. The problems sit at the seams between sections. First, the vertical-only decision lives only in an addendum: the runbook body, the master checklist, the S12 command and the root README pipeline line still instruct a 16:9 master, so following the checklist would produce a non-compliant video. Second, the 'human review = $0' decision exists only in 13 §7.13; the 08 workbooks, the 07/08 budget, RD-15 and the business pilot line still budget paid review. Third, section 13 is not registered in the decision log or the skills ownership map. Its cascade conflicts with AD-02, AD-11 and AD-24 and with the shipped effort governor. It lets derived Reels skip the GS approvals, uses a ±150 ms sync tolerance against the contract's 'never late' rule, and re-specifies as 'new' QA checks that anim-qa already owns. Fourth, the safe-zone geometry has three splits and three side margins across the tokens, layout script, QA and template. None of this breaks the strategy, but the founder should not treat the documents as one consistent end-to-end spec until F01–F10 are reconciled into 07/10 and the code tokens.

Partially aligned. On the arithmetic itself the work is very strong. I recomputed about 120 numbers in 13 STRATEGY §7.3–7.13, the experiment protocol, and 08 CONSOLIDATED Parts A–E (v1, v2, narration, business, reconciliation), and all of them check out apart from rounding. The [V1] figures match the Devarf transcript exactly. A sample of about 37 quoted claims in the 11 PLAYBOOK and the 12 RESEARCH_REPORT matches the SOURCES files, with contested items honestly labelled. Skill counts (57 + 15 = 72, matrix 72 rows), the engine's 56 tests and the README file counts are correct. The problems are in framing and stale cross-references, and some of them would mislead the founder on exactly the cost-control and vertical-only goals. First, the text says 40–100× on total cost is reached at the lean floor, but the document's own table tops out at 7× against an Opus Kit and 27× against bespoke generation (F1). Second, the 'Today' baseline is priced at old 4.6-era tariffs while the cascade uses the verified 5.5 prices (F2). Third, the lean floor uses a TTS price that doubles on 1 Jan 2027 (F4). Fourth, the narration test gates still say '57 passed' after the fix that makes it 58 passed plus 2 FFmpeg failures (F3). Fifth, the master README's pipeline line still says 16:9 master and 9:16 recompose (F5). Sixth, the 08 cost models and the runbook's cost-tracking chapter never record the $0-review decision (F6). Fix these six and the cost and evidence layer will be accurate and goal-aligned.

PARTIALLY ALIGNED. Every ask has a real deliverable. (1) Nothing from the ChatGPT source is missing: every downloaded and extracted file is in the sections, verified by hash. (2) The human-feel research directly answers the jingle question and the 'emotion then dub' question, and covers Hindi. (3) The animation layer uses all five videos, has all 65 edge cases with owners, 15 complete skills whose selftests all pass, and a deterministic harness. (4) The Indic tokenizer fix is correct and documented. (5) The strong-to-cheap strategy includes the protocol, templates, timeline and a correct review-free addendum. The weak point is end-to-end integration. Sections 11, 12 and 13 sit beside the master runbook (07) and cost docs (08) instead of being folded into them. As a result, the founder's single checklist still renders 16:9 masters, has no storyboard gate, no ultracode ban and no AI-disclosure gate, still budgets human review as cash, and still quotes a narration gate of '57 passed' that the fix has made wrong. One real interface defect also blocks execution: the cue-sheet builder does not produce the schema the harness requires. Ultracode policy also conflicts across the edge table, the governor script and the experiment protocol. The 'YouTube tricks/tutorials' and microdrama-pacing parts of ask 2 are only thinly answered. Fix F1–F7 (mostly propagation edits plus one code fix) and the project is aligned.

Partially aligned. The pieces themselves work. All 26 offline selftests pass. The harness tools and their skill copies are byte-identical. The template passes the strict lint. Skill frontmatter is valid. Every key file path exists, and only 6 of 283 relative links are dead, all of them ChatGPT sandbox links. The animation setup document is careful about marking unsourced HyperFrames/Remotion commands as 'verify' and gets this Mac's blockers right. Following the operating documents end to end, though, still leads the engineer astray in four places. (1) The master checklist and the per-lesson procedure still tell them to render 16:9 1920×1080 masters, against the vertical-only decision, and the animation-layer setup, S-ANIM gate and storyboard gate (H-SB) are missing from the checklist because the PA-17/PA-03 amendments were never applied. (2) The setup gates expect '57 passed' for narration, but the suite now has 60 cases (58 pass without FFmpeg). (3) The primary setup document understates this Mac's blockers: ffmpeg is missing, not just ffprobe; Node 20 is not mentioned; Node 24 is already available via nvm. Its venv commands also create Python 3.14 environments here, or fail because `python` does not exist. (4) preflight.sh is credited with secret, ultracode, model-pin and Manim checks it does not have, and no render command exists for the determinism gate. A competent engineer can get from an empty machine to the engine and narration proofs with small corrections. They cannot complete the animation-layer gate, or produce compliant vertical output from the checklist alone, until these items are fixed.

Partially aligned. In the core runbook (07) and the animation layer (12), the science-safety non-negotiables are mostly well specified and the code backs them up. Science glyphs come only from fixtures, checked through data-fx and the text diff. Image models are banned from producing text. Agents cannot research facts. GA/GF/GS approvals bind to hashes and need different reviewers. Fake sensing and hype are banned, and answers stay hidden. Voice consent, DPDP caution, the licence ledger and the ultracode ban are in place. There are no secrets in the repo, and entitlement stays with the platform. All the offline selftests I ran pass. The gaps appear where the newer documents (11 PLAYBOOK, 13 STRATEGY) meet the runbook. Two of them would produce non-compliant output if followed. First, 13 §5.7 lets LLM-written Reel hooks ship on an 'inherited' approval and one short human check, which removes GS. Second, AI-voice disclosure is enforced by no gate, check or export field, and the suggested wording would mislead on Path B TTS content. Several majors also need fixing before use. The playbook's 3 s pause cap undercuts the 6 s think window. Path A lets the performer change approved wording without re-approval. anim-qa lets a human waive untraceable science text and full-frame flashes. The kit verifier stack and diagram drop the A-suite checks and the storyboard gate. The storyboard approval record has a single role, can be forged by the agent, and lacks fixture hashes. Fix these and the pipeline would be aligned with the founder's non-negotiables.

Partially aligned. The core design matches what the founder wants: fixture-only science, verifier-only advancement, two human gates, ultracode banned, honest 'not yet run' banners, and a sound Kit-first idea for moving work from strong models to cheap ones. But the project is mostly documents about documents. There are about 712k words of markdown and 72 skills (none agent-evaluated, 15 of which cannot be used without another skill). The harness contract is written three times, there are five house styles, two divergent cue-sheet validators, two reference analysers, three pilot programmes, about five ledgers, and a 20-arm, 185-engineer-hour campaign. All of this sits on a machine that cannot render a single frame yet. Worse, the files people actually work from (the master checklist, the per-lesson procedure, the root pipeline line) still say 16:9 and have no storyboard gate. The $0-review decision and the section-13 strategy never reached the runbook or cost docs. Section 13's own diagram puts academic approval after rendering. The headline savings are measured against a hypothetical Opus-only Kit and an older price set; at the same prices the saving against today's pipeline is about 2%. Before anything else, fix F1–F4 in place. Then merge the extenders into their owner skills, make one copy of each contract canonical, cut the campaign to 3 archetypes, and ship one vertical lesson end to end before writing more.

findings_kept.claim: The cost floors leave out the cost drivers of the craft the project chose: a human performer for every lesson, filmed teacher cutaways, and Higgsfield credits for paper-collage. The 'lean floor' is therefore a guess.
findings_kept.evidence: Lean floor "≈$0.59: Gemini-class TTS ≈$0.14 ... stills $0.20". 11 PLAYBOOK §5: "A real teacher performs the lesson. Speech-to-speech then converts..."; line 304: "1–3 short real teacher cutaways per lesson". 07/04 line 228: S2S "$0.12 per generated minute (before performer and review)". 12 doc 05: Higgsfield "per-model credit costs are not verified (Q5)", "There's no native credit cap", and the collage style is "on the expensive side regarding credits". The performer is also a second capacity limit that the 85-minute math leaves out.
findings_kept.suggested_fix: Add performer minutes, cutaway filming and Higgsfield credits per style as explicit (unknown) lines. State that the lean floor applies only to Path-B TTS lessons with no paid stills.

findings_kept.claim: The go thresholds treat 5 correlated samples per scene as independent, which overstates confidence. A review-minutes gate uses an assumed baseline as if it had been measured.
findings_kept.evidence: §6.4: "The scene is the unit; the 5 samples of one scene are correlated." Yet §6.5's first gate is "Sample-level final pass ... Wilson LB ≥ 0.90 (≥ 115/120)". "Pilot human review minutes | Not above the 85-minute baseline": 85 min is a workbook planning assumption (07/README:75), never timed.
findings_kept.suggested_fix: Gate on scene-level counts (or a cluster-adjusted interval) only. Label the 85-minute figure as a hypothesis and record the measured pilot minutes as the baseline.
